upper_bound.witness: The entire necessity argument rests on estimate (7), |d(y)-d(t)| <= (y-t)^2/(4 min{t,y}) for all t,y>0. The text does not prove it: it announces that squaring and rearranging the two inequalities at x = f(t) = t+c gives (7) and then explicitly omits the details. What would have to be shown, for all t,y>0 with b=d(y), c=d(t): from 2((t+c)^2+(y+b)^2) >= (t+2c+y)^2 and (t+2c+y)^2 >= 4(t+c)(y+b), together with b,c >= 0, derive the two-sided bound on |b-c|. No such derivation (nor any case analysis, e.g. b>c versus c>b, or the fixed-point case b=0) appears in the write-up.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Section 3's telescoping/partition argument uses (7) as its only input, so the conclusion that d is constant (and hence f(x)=x+C, including the exclusion of mixed fixed-point/shift behaviour) stands or falls entirely with the omitted derivation of (7).

parsed.notes: Answer set and range of C correct. Substitution x=f(y) correctly yields f(f(y))+y=2f(y), the orbit formula and d>=0. Sufficiency verified for all x,y and all C>=0 via RMS-AM-GM on x and y+C. The key local estimate (7) driving necessity is asserted with 'details omitted'.
